newsitem.title: USA: New Haven, Conn., mayor calls for tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: New Haven, Conn., mayor calls for tax cuts.

text.p: New Haven Mayor John DeStefano, Jr., told a news conference late Wednesday that he would seek a 24-mill reduction in the city tax rate and a $9-million cut in the amount of taxes the city collects.
He said the city would accomplish this by virtue of the $9 million in unbudgeted state revenues as a result of the recently approved state budget.
DeStefano proposed to pass on every dollar to city taxpayers in the form of direct property tax relief.
The additional state aid would be applied directly to lowering the mill rate to 37 mills from 61 mills, he said.
This would put New Haven on a par with area towns and make it more affordable than most big Connecticut cities, he said.
DeStefano also proposed that the city complete the implementation of the 1991 revaluation, which had been frozen since 1994.
The mayor noted that the last time New Haven's mill rate was under 38 mills was 1960.
DeStefano, a Democrat, is expected to announce on Thursday afternoon that he will seek a third term as mayor this November.
